claims.text: In-situ TEM during high-temperature oxidation can elucidate oxidation mechanisms in Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 produced by additive manufacturing.
In-situ TEM during oxidation can reveal elemental redistribution associated with nanoprecipitates in this alloy.
In-situ XRD during high-temperature oxidation can elucidate oxidation mechanisms in this alloy.
In-situ XRD during oxidation can reveal elemental redistribution associated with nanoprecipitates in this alloy.
The initial material is additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 with dual nanoprecipitation.
The proposed oxidation experiment is conducted at 800°C in air or oxygen for 100 hours.
High-temperature oxidation induces elemental redistribution in the alloy.
High-temperature oxidation induces phase transformation in the alloy.
The additively manufactured alloy will have a 20% lower oxidation rate than its cast and wrought counterparts.
Oxidation will produce a 30% increase in nanoprecipitate number density relative to the cast and wrought counterparts.
The comparison baseline is cast and wrought Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
The proposed hypothesis is intended to apply from 700°C to 900°C in air or oxygen.
Variations in additive-manufacturing process parameters can alter the resulting microstructure and nanoprecipitate distribution.
Changes in microstructure and nanoprecipitate distribution can affect oxidation resistance.
The hypothesis is falsified if oxidation rate is not reduced by at least 15% or nanoprecipitate density does not increase by at least 20% relative to cast and wrought counterparts.
